items.q: Match each urine feature of RPGN with its description — 1) Colour  2) Output  3) Urine analysis … A) Decreased output  B) Cola-coloured (RBC present)  C) Proteinuria +/– (trace to variable)
items.exp: RPGN urine: cola-coloured with RBCs; decreased output; urine examination shows proteinuria +/–. (Book p778)

items.q: A 40-year-old man has a 3-week history of progressive puffiness around the eyes and legs, BP 160/100 mmHg, cola-coloured urine and reduced urine output. Which statement about these findings is correct?
opts: Periorbital puffiness with progressive oedema and a raised BP are listed features of RPGN
Periorbital puffiness with a normal BP is a feature unique to nephrotic syndrome
The progressive oedema of RPGN accumulates in the intravascular compartment
Cola-coloured urine with reduced output indicates isolated post-renal obstruction
items.exp: RPGN features: periorbital puffiness, progressive oedema (extravascular compartment) and raised blood pressure, with cola-coloured urine and decreased output. (Book p778)

items.q: Fill up: In RPGN, progressive oedema accumulates in the ______ compartment.
opts: extravascular
intravascular
pericardial
cerebrospinal
items.exp: Features of RPGN: progressive oedema (extravascular compartment), periorbital puffiness and raised blood pressure. (Book p778)

items.q: Raised blood pressure is a listed feature of RPGN along with periorbital puffiness.
opts: True
False — BP is normal in RPGN
True, but only in type III disease
False — BP falls as creatinine rises
items.exp: RPGN features list ends with raised blood pressure. (Book p778)

items.q: A man with RPGN is examined. Chest auscultation is expected to reveal:
opts: Scattered crepitations
A pleural rub with absent breath sounds
A pansystolic murmur at the apex
Bronchial breathing with a pleural rub
items.exp: Auscultation in RPGN: scattered crepitations (from fluid overload/uraemic lung). (Book p778)

items.q: Which statement about blood investigations in RPGN is correct?
opts: CBC is normal, while serum creatinine and urea are raised
CBC shows marked leucocytosis, with normal creatinine
Serum creatinine is raised only if sepsis coexists
Serum urea is reduced with a raised creatinine
items.exp: Blood investigations in RPGN: CBC normal; serum creatinine raised; serum urea raised; serum K⁺ normal or raised; ABG normal or metabolic acidosis. (Book p778)

items.q: Match each RPGN investigation with its expected result — 1) CBC  2) Serum creatinine  3) Serum K⁺  4) ABG … A) Normal/raised  B) Normal  C) Normal/metabolic acidosis  D) Raised
items.exp: RPGN investigations: CBC normal; creatinine raised; serum K⁺ normal or raised; ABG normal or metabolic acidosis (serum urea also raised). (Book p778)

items.q: All but one of the following are typical laboratory findings in RPGN. Which is the odd one out?
opts: Normocytic anaemia with a low haemoglobin on the CBC
Raised serum creatinine together with a raised serum urea
Normal CBC with a raised serum creatinine and a raised urea
ABG showing normal pH or metabolic acidosis with normal or high K⁺
items.exp: The CBC is normal in RPGN; creatinine and urea are raised, serum K⁺ is normal or raised and the ABG is normal or shows metabolic acidosis. (Book p778)
